obligations.instructions: `item.text` is JSON: `statement` is one MUST or MUST NOT statement of the requirement record in `record`. Judge only `statement`; use `record` as context. How many independent obligations does this statement impose?

joined_by.instructions: `item.text` is JSON: `statement` is one MUST or MUST NOT statement of the requirement record in `record`. Judge only `statement`; use `record` as context. What joins its obligations?

criteria.and-list: A list of items joined by and or commas. Fix: split into one statement per item.
criteria.condition+obligation: A condition (when, if, unless) plus one obligation. Acceptable: a condition is not a second obligation.
criteria.alternatives: Alternatives joined by or. Fix: split, or state the choice.
criteria.obligation+rationale: An obligation plus its reason or purpose. Fix: move the rationale to Rationale.

term.instructions: `item.text` is JSON: `statement` is one MUST or MUST NOT statement of the requirement record in `record`. Judge only `statement`; use `record` as context. What kind of term in this statement is unclear?

criteria.none: Every term is common usage or defined in the record.
criteria.project term defined in a linked record: A project term defined in a record this one links. Acceptable.
criteria.project term defined nowhere: A project term defined neither here nor in a linked record. Fix: define it or link the record.
criteria.vague qualifier: A qualifier such as fast, clear or robust with no measure. Fix: replace it with a measure.
criteria.undefined acronym: An acronym that is never expanded or defined. Fix: define the acronym.

check.instructions: `item.text` is JSON: `statement` is one MUST or MUST NOT statement of the requirement record in `record`. Judge only `statement`; use `record` as context. What would check this statement?

criteria.CLI run: Running a command and reading its output or exit code.
criteria.inspection or grep: Reading or searching files or output.
criteria.needs a measure: A check exists only once a number is given. Fix: add a threshold.
criteria.none: Nothing could check it. Fix: rewrite as an outcome.

d_term_where.instructions: `item.text` is JSON: `statement` is one MUST or MUST NOT statement of the requirement record in `record`. Judge only `statement`; use `record` as context. If a word or phrase in `statement` is neither common usage nor defined in `record`, which kind is it?

criteria.none: Every word is common usage or defined in `record`.
criteria.actor: The subject that must act (a component, writer, crate or role).
criteria.artifact: A named type, crate, file, function, field, table or command.
criteria.reference: A back-reference such as that, it, this, the above, or the same.
criteria.condition: A word in the condition or trigger (when, if, before, after).
criteria.qualifier: An adjective or adverb (default, immediately, unrelated, canonical, exact).

d_term_fix.instructions: `item.text` is JSON: `statement` is one MUST or MUST NOT statement of the requirement record in `record`. Judge only `statement`; use `record` as context. What one change would most raise confidence that every term in `statement` is understood?

criteria.define in record: Add a one-sentence definition of the term to the record's definitions.
criteria.replace reference: Replace a back-reference (that, it, the same) with the full noun phrase.
criteria.plain words: Replace jargon with plain words that say the same thing.
criteria.name the owner: Say which component or crate the named thing belongs to.

d_check_why.instructions: `item.text` is JSON: `statement` is one MUST or MUST NOT statement of the requirement record in `record`. Judge only `statement`; use `record` as context. What would a tester most need, to know how to check `statement`?

criteria.nothing: How to check it is already clear.
criteria.observable: The observable outcome (an error, a returned value, a file or row content).
criteria.location: Where to look (the file, crate, command or table).
criteria.trigger: The input or event that triggers the obligation.
criteria.test kind: Whether it is checked by a test, a command, or reading the code.

d_obligations_why.instructions: `item.text` is JSON: `statement` is one MUST or MUST NOT statement of the requirement record in `record`. Judge only `statement`; use `record` as context. If `statement` could be read as more than one obligation, what causes that?

criteria.single: It reads as exactly one obligation.
criteria.ordering: An ordering word (before, after, immediately) adds a second duty.
criteria.condition: A condition hides a second duty.
criteria.list: A list or the word and joins several things.
criteria.default: A default plus an exception or override.

d_ambiguous.instructions: `item.text` is JSON: `statement` is one MUST or MUST NOT statement of the requirement record in `record`. Judge only `statement`; use `record` as context. Is any phrase in `statement` open to two readings?

criteria.quantifier: The scope of every, any, each or all.
criteria.reference: What that, it, this or the same refers to.
criteria.noun: A noun that could mean two different things.

d_check_kind.instructions: `item.text` is JSON: `statement` is one MUST or MUST NOT statement of the requirement record in `record`. Judge only `statement`; use `record` as context. Is the obligation about what the software does when run, or about what files contain?

criteria.runtime: Behaviour when run: a returned value, an error, an exit code, a written row or output.
criteria.static: Content of files: a manifest key, a dependency edge, a file existing or its text.
criteria.both: It mixes runtime behaviour and file content.
criteria.unclear: It does not say what observable decides it.
